history.summary: TOWN CORRECTION: the CSV town 'Ganpatipule' is wrong — the temple is in the village of Ganeshgule (also called Agargule/Aagargule), Ratnagiri district, ~22 km from Ratnagiri town. This small lateritic-stone Ganesh temple is said to be about 400 years old, older than the Ganpatipule temple, with a dome in a pre-Shivaji style. There is no carved idol; a naturally formed (self-stylised) rock is worshipped as Ganesha. Folklore ties it directly to the Ganpatipule legend: Gule was the god's original abode, and when the holy water that once flowed from Ganesh's navel (as tirtha from the Gomukh) suddenly stopped, devotees believed the god had moved on to Ganpatipule. A 70-foot-deep step well carved into the lateritic plateau near the temple is a local marvel (one source calls it 'Pandav era' — traditional claim, verify). The site is quiet and surrounded by forest. COORDINATES ARE APPROXIMATE (village-level geocode). NO RELIABLE IMAGE: genuine searching found only the Ganpatipule temple mislabelled or a video title card; the one page-specific photo host refused all fetches, so media is intentionally empty.

name: Ganeshgule (Agargule) Temple
town_description: Ganeshgule (Agargule) is a small coastal village in Ratnagiri district on Maharashtra's Konkan coast, best known as the original abode of Ganapati in the folklore that gave Ganpatipule its name. The village lies about 22 km from Ratnagiri town, roughly 4 km off the Purnagad road from Pawas, set amid coconut groves and lateritic plateaus typical of the Konkan landscape. It remains a quiet, little-visited pilgrim spot in contrast to the busy Ganpatipule shrine nearby.
